citation.title: Studies of the halo effect in the charge exchange recombination spectroscopy edge measurements at ITER
citation.authors: Pavlova G S, Serov S V, Tugarinov S N, von Hellerman M

topic: Simulated contribution of beam-halo charge exchange to ITER CXRS Edge line intensity, line shape, and spatial resolution, using the SOS code.
own_question: How much could the beam halo bias ITER edge CXRS density, temperature, and velocity measurements, and how much could it degrade their spatial resolution?
actual_method_and_evidence: This is a simulation-only study. The authors used the SOS code with a diffusion model of the halo. They simulated a 100 keV hydrogen beam for three ITER scenarios over 0.5≤ρ≤1. They report that the halo raises line intensity by up to 20% for impurities and 32% for deuterium. They report Ti and velocity shifts under 1%. They report spatial-resolution loss of about 1.5 cm for He and 2.5 cm for D. They propose an atomic-data uncertainty bound of 20% as a conservative estimate. No experimental data and no KSTAR data were used.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Beam-halo charge exchange can add emission outside the beam–sightline intersection, which can affect the locality of CXRS measurements.
claim_checks.qualification: Results are ITER simulations, not measurements. The magnitudes cannot be transferred to KSTAR carbon CES.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. The paper contains no temporal, causal, or nowcasting content.
validation_if_relevant: Model-based error estimates only. There is no experimental validation and no data split.
forbidden_inferences: That KSTAR CES labels carry halo biases of these magnitudes.
That halo effects explain errors in our nowcasting.
That ITER requirements apply to KSTAR.
That these results are demonstrated, rather than simulated, performance.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional at most. It could support one theory sentence noting that CES labels are model-dependent conventional reports rather than independent truth. It is not needed for the causal-nowcasting framing.
